description:
FOUND s501 (Fable, 2026-09-29) by the review probe for s494h (#2006 b) -- PRE-EXISTING on main 558cc5a0, NOT caused by s494h.  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/review/sc3.pl; perl prints `1 5 5`, PCL prints `1 0 5`):
    { open(my $h, ">", "$f.n") or die; sub usesh { print $h "named" } sub closeh { close $h } }
    { open(my $h, ">", $f) or die; print $h "other"; close $h; }
    usesh(); closeh();
    print "1 ", -s "$f.n", " ", -s $f, "\n";
The two `my $h` are DIFFERENT variables in perl.  PCL emits ONE cell `(p-defcell $h (make-p-box nil))` (an IDENTITY promotion, no `__file__N` rename) and the second block's `open(my $h ...)` has NO `p-let` -- it re-opens the captured cell, so the named sub's handle is closed and replaced; `usesh()` then prints to a closed handle and the text is lost.

WHAT IS MEASURED (each probe perl vs main, files beside sc3.pl):
- sc5.pl: the same without `or die` -- same wrong.  So the `or` is not the trigger.
- sc6.pl: captured declaration spelled `my $h; open($h, ...)` (statement-level my) -- RIGHT.
- sc7.pl / sc8.pl: the same shape with a USER sub (`foo(my $v)`) as captured declaration or as sibling -- RIGHT: the captured one is renamed `$v__file__0` and every sibling gets its `p-let`.
- sc4 (in this task only): captured `my $x = 1` with siblings `f(my $x = 5) or die`, `(my $x = 6) or die`, `defined(my $x = 8) || die` -- RIGHT.
=> the trigger is the captured declaration being the embedded `my` of an `open(...)` BUILTIN call in a file-level block, captured by a NAMED sub: the promoter takes the identity route and the same-name sibling declarations in other file-level blocks (bare block, loop body, if branch -- v2.pl shows all three; a sibling inside a SUB is right) are then not bound.  Look for the place where `open(my $fh` at file level is treated by NAME (grep Parser2 for the identity-promotion decision and for an open-specific declaration path); detector / rewriter / promoter must share ONE resolver (standing rule).  Siblings probed only for `open`; probe `opendir(my $d`, `pipe(my $r, my $w)`, `socket(my $s`, `read($fh, my $buf, N)`, `sysopen(my $h`, `chomp(my $l = <FH>)` as captured declaration too -- the family may be "embedded my with NO assignment as a builtin's argument".

SECOND SYMPTOM, in s494h's tree only: the handle licence's F-DEBUG line says CLOSED for such a sibling while NO `p-scope-close` is emitted (m2.pl, v2.pl: verdict count 2-3, emission count 0-1) -- the verdict is computed for a declaration the emission never binds.  Reported to s494h as a review finding (the verdict must say so); the scoping bug itself is THIS task.

BAR: a rename/scoping change => the full sweep IS the gate (#296), `--quick` companion once, gate-SET scan over both populations; guard rows with sc3's shape + the three sibling kinds; ~10 probes vs perl incl. the breaking case (a file-level `open(my $h` captured by a named sub with NO same-name sibling must stay byte-identical in emission).

=== WIDENED s501 (Fable, 2026-09-30, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/review/r501b-scope.pl; perl and base outputs in out/) ===
The family is NOT open-specific: the trigger is the CAPTURED declaration being an EMBEDDED `my` in a call argument, WITH OR WITHOUT an assignment.  Measured on main 77212b1f, each a named sub capturing the embedded `my` of one block and a same-name sibling in another block:
  row 1  open(my $h ...)                  the named sub`s file prints 0 bytes (perl 5): sibling re-opened the captured cell
  row 2  opendir(my $dh ...)              nextent() answers 0 (perl 1): the sibling`s closedir closed the captured handle
  row 3b pipe(my $r, my $w)              rd() answers nothing (perl `piped`)
  row 4  read($in, my $buf, 3)           getbuf() answers the SIBLING`s bytes `su` (perl `oth`)
  row 5  chomp(my $line = "cap\n")       getline_() answers `sib` (perl `cap`) -- an embedded my WITH an assignment
  row 7  sysopen(my $sh ...)              sysrd() answers nothing (perl `other`)
  row 6  my ($p, $q); captured, sibling `my ($p, $q) = (3, 4)`   RIGHT (statement-level declarations)
So: every embedded `my` that a named sub captures takes the identity promotion, and a sibling embedded `my` of the same name is then the same cell.  Acceptance for the fix = r501b-scope.pl identical to perl.


=== DONE (s501b) ===
Why the embedded shape missed: `_scan_lex_facts` offers only top-level declarations to the capture promoter, so a `my` embedded in a PLAIN statement's arguments fell to `_lower_block`'s embedded-`my` VETO -- one forward-defvar'd global for the NAME.  Fix (Pl/Parser2.pm): `_embedded_decl_candidates` pairs every plain statement at the top of its extent with each declarator from `_embedded_my_syms` (the ONE embedded-decl reading the lowering already uses) and hands them to `_promote_captured` with `$emb_sym`: renamed `$h__file__N`, only the declarator renamed inside its own statement (perl introduces the name after the statement), the cell published by `_lower_block`'s embedded arm (`_emb_promoted`); every same-name sibling then keeps its own `p-let` (and scope close).  The identity case and a decl with a later string eval naming it DECLINE (`_caprefuse`) -- they keep today's veto-path single cell.
Acceptance: review r501b-scope 9/9 == perl (rows 1 2 3b 4 5 7 fixed; 3 6 8 stay right); sc3/sc5 == perl; brk1 (a lone file-level captured `open(my $h`) emission byte-identical; the #2006(b) licence agrees with the emission (F-DEBUG CLOSED count == emitted p-scope-close: m2 2=2, v2 3=3).
Guards: Pl/t/fh-scope-close-01.t section 2b (rows 56-67; 12 fail on the a0899ba6 code).  Scoping bars: gate-set-scan over BOTH populations 638 files IDENTICAL; full sweep TOTAL 18714 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed, GATE clean, drops 5 = census; companion --all --quick + a 120-file A/B vs a0899ba6: no mover from this member.  ir-spec §2b.3 (normative).
subject: A named sub capturing a block's `open(my $h ...)` makes every same-name `open(my $h ...)` in other file-level blocks share ONE cell (silent wrong; pre-existing)
